title: Finite-Time Simulation of the Source Machine
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-alphabet Turing machine with $k>0$ work tapes, choose a source symbol $a_0$, and let $x$ be a finite word over the enlarged sweep alphabet. Fix a time $	au$ such that the source machine, started on the word obtained by retracting each symbol of $x$, is nonhalted at every time $t<\tau$. For every $t\le\tau$, there are integers $a$ and natural numbers $n,u$ such that the source configuration at time $t$ has a window of $n$ consecutive work-tape cells beginning at $a$, satisfying the head, blank-outside, visited-cell, size, and history conditions of a valid window; moreover, $u$ is at most the simulator time bound $\sigma_k(t)$, and by time $u$ the simulator started on $x$ reaches the encoded configuration built from that source configuration and window, while its work head stays throughout between $ak-1$ and $(a+n)k$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: decidable equality on the source alphabet
a finite Turing machine M with k>0 work tapes
the source run is nonhalted at every time t<τ
